skill.name: frontend-design
skill.description: Guides AI agents to design and implement distinctive, accessible, production-ready frontend interfaces with an explicit aesthetic direction and coherent design system.
skill.summary: Create memorable frontend interfaces with intentional visual direction, working code, accessibility, and performance standards.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All seven static findings are false positives. Lines 63 and 65 are Markdown fences around an arithmetic formula, while the remaining matches are ordinary design guidance. No prompt injection, command execution, reconnaissance, or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: * Avoid system fonts and AI-defaults (Inter, Roboto, Arial, etc.)

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 63 is an opening Markdown code fence for the DFII formula, not Ruby syntax or executable shell content. The enclosed text is arithmetic documentation.
Line 65 is the closing Markdown code fence for the documented DFII formula. It does not invoke a shell, Ruby interpreter, or external command.
Line 15 advises against generic AI interface patterns. It contains no instruction to inspect the host, collect system information, or perform reconnaissance.
The phrase "system fonts" on line 119 is a standard typography term. The line recommends font choices and does not request host enumeration.
Line 135 discusses balanced color palettes as a visual-design choice. It has no relation to system discovery or security-sensitive inspection.
The grid on line 139 is a page-layout grid, and the instruction concerns visual composition. No computing system or network is examined.
Line 158 discourages excessive decorative interface motion. It does not describe reconnaissance, data collection, or privileged behavior.

content.value_statement: Generic interface patterns weaken product identity and user impact. This skill guides AI agents to create distinctive, accessible frontends with coherent design systems and working code.
actual_capabilities: Defines purpose, audience, tone, and a differentiation anchor before implementation.
Scores design directions using aesthetic impact, context fit, feasibility, performance, and consistency risk.
Produces working HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or React interfaces with modular implementation guidance.
Creates typography, color, spacing, and motion rules for a cohesive design system.
Applies semantic HTML, contrast, focus, keyboard, and performance requirements.
limitations: Does not replace browser testing, usability research, accessibility audits, or performance profiling.
Requires product context and technical constraints to choose an appropriate aesthetic direction.
Does not provide bundled fonts, images, brand assets, or framework dependencies.
Strong stylistic rules may need adaptation for established design systems and regulated products.

use_cases.title: Shape a product concept
use_cases.description: Turn a product brief into a named visual direction, differentiation anchor, and practical design system.

use_cases.title: Implement a polished interface
use_cases.description: Build a responsive interface with coherent typography, color, spacing, motion, and accessible interaction states.

use_cases.title: Differentiate a launch page
use_cases.description: Create a memorable launch experience that reflects the product audience without relying on generic templates.

prompt_templates.title: Define a visual direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this product brief: [brief]. Define the purpose, audience, dominant tone, differentiation anchor, and DFII score before proposing implementation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the visual direction is still open.

prompt_templates.title: Design a focused page
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a [page type] for [audience]. Use [brand constraints], prioritize [primary action], and provide the direction, design system, and responsive behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a new page with clear product goals.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a complete interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the approved direction in [technology]. Include responsive layouts, semantic structure, keyboard access, focus states, performance considerations, and purposeful motion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when design direction and technical requirements are known.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and refine a design system
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this existing interface against its audience, aesthetic direction, accessibility needs, and performance goals. Identify generic patterns, then implement prioritized improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for advanced refinement of an existing product interface.

output_examples.input: Create a mobile-first portfolio for an editorial photographer.
output: Direction: archival editorial with high-contrast typography and asymmetrical image pacing.
System: expressive serif headings, restrained body text, black, paper white, and signal red.
Implementation: responsive gallery, keyboard navigation, visible focus states, optimized images, and restrained page transitions.

output_examples.input: Redesign a logistics dashboard for dispatch operators.
output: Direction: industrial utility focused on scanning, comparison, and rapid exception handling.
System: compact typography, neutral surfaces, status colors, stable table geometry, and sparse motion.
Implementation: responsive data views, keyboard workflows, clear alerts, accessible contrast, and persistent operational context.

output_examples.input: Improve a generic software launch page without changing its content.
output: Direction: precise technical editorial with a strong typographic hierarchy and product-first composition.
Differentiation: replace repeated feature cards with a structured product walkthrough and one memorable interaction.
Validation: verify mobile text fit, keyboard navigation, image clarity, motion preferences, and loading performance.

best_practices: Provide the audience, primary action, content, brand constraints, technology, and performance requirements.
Choose one dominant aesthetic direction and one memorable differentiation anchor before implementation.
Test the generated interface across devices, keyboard workflows, reduced motion settings, and production data.
anti_patterns: Combining unrelated visual styles without a clear product rationale.
Using default fonts, balanced palettes, repeated cards, and predictable sections as the final design.
Adding animation, texture, or decorative effects that reduce clarity, accessibility, or performance.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a design direction, design system guidance, working frontend implementation, and a clear differentiation rationale.

faq.question: Which frontend technologies can it use?
faq.answer: It supports native HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and React guidance. Other technologies require clear project context.

faq.question: Does it address accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires semantic structure, sufficient contrast, visible focus, keyboard access, and restrained motion.

faq.question: Can it extend an existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide current components, tokens, brand rules, and constraints so recommendations remain compatible.

faq.question: Does it include fonts and visual assets?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend appropriate choices, but projects must supply licenses, asset files, and loading configuration.

faq.question: How should generated work be validated?
faq.answer: Test it in target browsers and devices, then run accessibility, usability, visual regression, and performance checks.
